# PDF fixtures of the extractor's tests

Two PDFs of known tools, for `tests/layout/known_tools.rs` (LAB-003), and what poppler, an independent PDF reader, found in them. The tests compile them in (they are listed in `DATA_FILES` in `xtask/src/verify.rs`), so they also run in WebAssembly; the fuzzing workflow uses the PDFs as seeds of the `pdf_extract` target.

| File | What it is | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `libreoffice.fodt` | The source of `libreoffice.pdf`: a flat OpenDocument text written for these tests, in Liberation Serif 12 pt. Two pages: left-to-right text with kerning, larger text, letter spacing and a superscript; two right-to-left Hebrew paragraphs, one with numbers and a Latin word; a left-to-right paragraph with a Hebrew word; a paragraph border; a two-by-two table with borders. | `5fabccb1d9f3d5bb269f71d63afc02044c39405ef638525d4f44e6984f3e3e74` |
| `libreoffice.pdf` | `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf libreoffice.fodt`, LibreOffice 24.2.7 (Ubuntu 24.04's `libreoffice-core` 4:24.2.7-0ubuntu0.24.04.7), with the Liberation fonts 2.1.5 (`fonts-liberation2`). It embeds a subset of Liberation Serif. | `bb1bf368688c4dbb81b804d155100a92d61a1526be8fb4e495a5640711a6cd37` |
| `chromium.html` | The source of `chromium.pdf`: an HTML page written for these tests, in Liberation Sans 11 pt: justified text, letter spacing, word spacing, a subscript and a superscript, two right-to-left Hebrew paragraphs, an inline image (an 8 × 8 red PNG), a horizontal rule and a table with borders. | `ae5ae3d9e9145f04784c247a51b65f87462df6604c5c8e4621de6341e17ac2d6` |
| `chromium.pdf` | Printed with Playwright 1.63.0's Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (Skia/PDF m153): `page.pdf({ format: 'A4', printBackground: true, preferCSSPageSize: true })`. It embeds a subset of Liberation Sans. | `916d22998ffc4509118fbf45f9241b2e92104bfb4e8ef74dcb85e4ae3018e7bc` |
| `libreoffice.words`, `chromium.words` | The words that poppler's `pdftotext -bbox` (poppler-utils 24.02.0) finds in each PDF, one per line: the page (from 1), the word's left and right edges in points, and the word, separated by tabs. A right-to-left word is in display order. | `6293322330b235a4480c52378f9a4b3d1182b4ea4e199db9f7830cc81c7d4304`, `ae93982f960933e389f6837485579c920515020d3132cf5324ae9cc374c4b136` |

The `.words` files were written from `pdftotext -bbox FILE.pdf FILE.html` by taking, from each `<word xMin=… yMin=… xMax=… yMax=…>` element, the page, `xMin`, `xMax` and the word with its HTML entities decoded. poppler places a word from its first glyph's origin to the end of its last glyph's advance, as the layout JSON does, so the tests compare those edges with the extracted glyphs within 0.01 pt; poppler's `yMin` and `yMax` come from the font's ascent and descent rather than the baseline, so the tests do not use them.

The documents use only fonts under the SIL Open Font License (Liberation Serif and Liberation Sans, which also cover Hebrew), so the font subsets embedded in the PDFs may be redistributed; `REUSE.toml` records it. The PDFs carry no personal data: their metadata names only the producing program, the time they were made and, in `chromium.pdf`, the HTML page's title.

To make them again, install the Liberation fonts, convert `libreoffice.fodt` with LibreOffice as above, and print `chromium.html` with Chromium as above; then regenerate the `.words` files and the samples (`BAYAN_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p bayan-lab-layout --test layout`), and review the difference. A new version of either program may lay the documents out differently, which changes the expected lines in `known_tools.rs` too.
